This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# What is Miller?

**Miller is like awk, sed, cut, join, and sort for data formats such as CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines, and positionally-indexed.**

# What can Miller do for me?

With Miller, you get to use named fields without needing to count positional
indices, using familiar formats such as CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines, and
positionally-indexed. Then, on the fly, you can add new fields which are
functions of existing fields, drop fields, sort, aggregate statistically,
pretty-print, and more.

* Miller operates on **key-value-pair data** while the familiar
Unix tools operate on integer-indexed fields: if the natural data structure for
the latter is the array, then Miller's natural data structure is the
insertion-ordered hash map.

* Miller handles a **variety of data formats**,
including but not limited to the familiar **CSV**, **TSV**, and **JSON**/**JSON Lines**.
(Miller can handle **positionally-indexed data** too!)

# Features

* Miller is **multi-purpose**: it's useful for **data cleaning**,
**data reduction**, **statistical reporting**, **devops**, **system
administration**, **log-file processing**, **format conversion**, and
**database-query post-processing**.

* You can use Miller to snarf and munge **log-file data**, including selecting
out relevant substreams, then produce CSV format and load that into
all-in-memory/data-frame utilities for further statistical and/or graphical
processing.

* Miller complements **data-analysis tools** such as **R**, **pandas**, etc.:
you can use Miller to **clean** and **prepare** your data. While you can do
**basic statistics** entirely in Miller, its streaming-data feature and
single-pass algorithms enable you to **reduce very large data sets**.

* Miller complements SQL **databases**: you can slice, dice, and reformat data
on the client side on its way into or out of a database. You can also reap some
of the benefits of databases for quick, setup-free one-off tasks when you just
need to query some data in disk files in a hurry.

* Miller also goes beyond the classic Unix tools by stepping fully into our
modern, **no-SQL** world: its essential record-heterogeneity property allows
Miller to operate on data where records with different schema (field names) are
interleaved.

* Miller is **streaming**: most operations need only a single record in
memory at a time, rather than ingesting all input before producing any output.
For those operations which require deeper retention (`sort`, `tac`, `stats1`),
Miller retains only as much data as needed. This means that whenever
functionally possible, you can operate on files which are larger than your
system's available RAM, and you can use Miller in **tail -f** contexts.

* Miller is **pipe-friendly** and interoperates with the Unix toolkit.

* Miller's I/O formats include **tabular pretty-printing**, **positionally
  indexed** (Unix-toolkit style), CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines, and others.

* Miller does **conversion** between formats.

* Miller's **processing is format-aware**: e.g. CSV `sort` and `tac` keep header lines first.

* Miller has high-throughput **performance** on par with the Unix toolkit.

# Usage

Miller operates on key-value-pair data while the familiar Unix tools operate
on integer-indexed fields: if the natural data structure for the latter is the
array, then Miller's natural data structure is the insertion-ordered hash map.
This encompasses a variety of data formats, including but not limited to the
familiar CSV, TSV, and JSON. (Miller can handle positionally-indexed data as
a special case.)

## Synopsis

```
mlr [flags] {verb} [verb-dependent options ...] {zero or more file names}
```

If zero file names are provided, standard input is read, e.g.:
```
mlr --csv sort -f shape example.csv
```

Output of one verb may be chained as input to another using "then", e.g.:
```
mlr --csv stats1 -a min,mean,max -f quantity then sort -f color example.csv
```

# License

Miller's license is two-clause BSD. See LICENSE.txt for details.
</output>

+------------+

</warning><output_head>
COMMENTS-IN-DATA FLAGS

Miller lets you put comments in your data, such as

    # This is a comment for a CSV file
    a,b,c
    1,2,3
    4,5,6

Notes:

* Comments are only honored at the start of a line.
* In the absence of any of the below four options, comments are data like
  any other text. (The comments-in-data feature is opt-in.)
* When `--pass-comments` is used, comment lines are written to standard output
  immediately upon being read; they are not part of the record stream.  Results
  may be counterintuitive. A suggestion is to place comments at the start of
  data files.

--pass-comments          Immediately print commented lines (prefixed by `#`)
                         within the input.
--pass-comments-with {string}
                         Immediately print commented lines within input, with
                         specified prefix. For CSV input format, the prefix
                         must be a single character.
--skip-comments          Ignore commented lines (prefixed by `#`) within the
                         input.
--skip-comments-with {string}
                         Ignore commented lines within input, with specified
                         prefix. For CSV input format, the prefix must be a
                         single character.

COMPRESSED-DATA FLAGS

Miller offers a few different ways to handle reading data files
	which have been compressed.

* Decompression done within the Miller process itself: `--bz2in` `--gzin` `--zin``--zstdin`
* Decompression done outside the Miller process: `--prepipe` `--prepipex`

Using `--prepipe` and `--prepipex` you can specify an action to be
taken on each input file.  The prepipe command must be able to read from
standard input; it will be invoked with `{command} < {filename}`.  The
prepipex command must take a filename as argument; it will be invoked with
`{command} {filename}`.

Examples:

    mlr --prepipe gunzip
    mlr --prepipe zcat -cf
    mlr --prepipe xz -cd
    mlr --prepipe cat

Note that this feature is quite general and is not limited to decompression
utilities. You can use it to apply per-file filters of your choice.  For output
compression (or other) utilities, simply pipe the output:
`mlr ... | {your compression command} > outputfilenamegoeshere`

Lastly, note that if `--prepipe` or `--prepipex` is specified, it replaces any
decisions that might have been made based on the file suffix. Likewise,
`--gzin`/`--bz2in`/`--zin``--zin` are ignored if `--prepipe` is also specified.

--bz2in                  Uncompress bzip2 within the Miller process. Done by
                         default if file ends in `.bz2`.
--gzin                   Uncompress gzip within the Miller process. Done by
                         default if file ends in `.gz`.
--prepipe {decompression command}
                         You can, of course, already do without this for
                         single input files, e.g. `gunzip < myfile.csv.gz |
                         mlr ...`. Allowed at the command line, but not in
                         `.mlrrc` to avoid unexpected code execution.
--prepipe-bz2            Same as `--prepipe bz2`, except this is allowed in
                         `.mlrrc`.
--prepipe-gunzip         Same as `--prepipe gunzip`, except this is allowed in
                         `.mlrrc`.

cat > src/main.go <<'GOEOF'
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"runtime"
	"strings"
)

const (
	progName = "mlr"
	version  = "6.16.0"
)

// Global state derived from CLI flags.

type opts struct {
	iFmt string
	oFmt string
	opt  *FormatOptions

	fromFiles []string
	mfromFiles []string
	noInput   bool

	csvLite bool

	implicitCSVHeader bool

	allowRaggedCSV bool
	csvTrimLS      bool
}

func newOpts() *opts {
	return &opts{
		iFmt: "dkvp",
		oFmt: "dkvp",
		opt: &FormatOptions{
			IFS: "", IPS: "", OFS: "", OPS: "", IRS: "", ORS: "",
			Flatsep: ".",
		},
	}
}

func main() {
	args := os.Args[1:]
	if len(args) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr: no verb supplied.")
		printUsage(os.Stderr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Handle top-level "pseudo-verbs".
	switch args[0] {
	case "--version":
		fmt.Printf("mlr %s\n", version)
		return
	case "version":
		fmt.Printf("mlr version %s for %s/%s/%s\n", version, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH, "go1.24.0")
		return
	case "--help", "-h", "help":
		handleHelp(args)
		return
	case "-l":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "-L":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "-g":
		// fallback: run help flags (not fully implemented)
		return
	}

	o := newOpts()
	rest, err := parseMainFlags(o, args)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr: no verb supplied.")
		printUsage(os.Stderr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Parse verb chain.
	var chain []Verb
	var files []string
	verbArgs := rest
	for len(verbArgs) > 0 {
		verbName := verbArgs[0]
		verbArgs = verbArgs[1:]
		v, remaining, err := buildVerb(verbName, verbArgs)
		if err != nil {
			if hr, ok := err.(helpRequest); ok {
				printVerbHelp(hr.verb, os.Stdout)
				return
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr %s: %s\n", verbName, err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		chain = append(chain, v)
		// Look for "then" in remaining; otherwise remaining = files (for last verb)
		if idx := indexOf(remaining, "then"); idx >= 0 {
			// remaining[:idx] are stray (probably files only allowed after last verb).
			files = append(files, remaining[:idx]...)
			verbArgs = remaining[idx+1:]
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, remaining...)
		break
	}

	// Input files from --from / --mfrom
	allFiles := append([]string{}, o.fromFiles...)
	allFiles = append(allFiles, o.mfromFiles...)
	allFiles = append(allFiles, files...)

	if err := runPipeline(o, chain, allFiles); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func printUsage(w io.Writer) {
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Usage: mlr [flags] {verb} [verb-dependent options ...] {zero or more file names}")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "If zero file names are provided, standard input is read, e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv sort -f shape example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Output of one verb may be chained as input to another using \"then\", e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv stats1 -a min,mean,max -f quantity then sort -f color example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please see 'mlr help topics' for more information.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please also see https://miller.readthedocs.io")
}

func handleHelp(args []string) {
	// args[0] is "help" or "--help" etc.
	if args[0] == "--help" || args[0] == "-h" {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	if len(args) == 1 {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	topic := args[1]
	switch topic {
	case "topics":
		printHelpTopics(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "list-verbs":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "usage-verbs":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "verb":
		if len(args) < 3 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr help verb: verb name required")
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		printVerbHelp(args[2], os.Stdout)
		return
	case "basic-examples":
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint cat example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint sort -f shape example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint sort -f shape -nr index example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint cut -f flag,shape example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --csv filter '$color == \"red\"' example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --ojson put '$ratio = $quantity / $rate' example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint --from example.csv sort -nr index then cut -f shape,quantity")
		return
	}
	// Default: print usage.
	printUsage(os.Stdout)
}

func printHelpTopics(w io.Writer) {
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Type 'mlr help {topic}' for any of the following:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Essentials:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help topics")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help basic-examples")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help file-formats")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Verbs:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help list-verbs")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help usage-verbs")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help verb")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Shorthands:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr -l = mlr help list-verbs")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr -L = mlr help usage-verbs")
}

func listVerbs(w io.Writer) {
	verbs := []string{
		"cat",
		"check",
		"count-distinct",
		"count",
		"cut",
		"filter",
		"group-by",
		"head",
		"label",
		"nothing",
		"put",
		"regularize",
		"rename",
		"reorder",
		"skip-trivial-records",
		"sort",
		"tac",
		"tail",
		"uniq",
	}
	bw := bufio.NewWriter(w)
	defer bw.Flush()
	for _, v := range verbs {
		bw.WriteString(v)
		bw.WriteString("\n")
	}
}

func listUsageVerbs(w io.Writer) {
	verbs := []string{
		"cat",
		"check",
		"count-distinct",
		"count",
		"cut",
		"filter",
		"group-by",
		"head",
		"label",
		"nothing",
		"put",
		"regularize",
		"rename",
		"reorder",
		"skip-trivial-records",
		"sort",
		"tac",
		"tail",
		"uniq",
	}
	for _, v := range verbs {
		printVerbHelp(v, w)
	}
}

func parseMainFlags(o *opts, args []string) ([]string, error) {
	i := 0
	for i < len(args) {
		a := args[i]
		// Format shortcuts.
		switch a {
		case "--csv", "-c", "--c2c":
			o.iFmt = "csv"
			o.oFmt = "csv"
			i++
			continue
		case "--csvlite":
			o.iFmt = "csv"
			o.oFmt = "csv"
			o.csvLite = true
			i++
			continue
		case "--tsv", "-t", "--t2t":
			o.iFmt = "tsv"
			o.oFmt = "tsv"
			i++
			continue
		case "--tsvlite":
			o.iFmt = "tsv"
			o.oFmt = "tsv"
			o.csvLite = true
			i++
			continue
		case "--dkvp", "--d2d":
			o.iFmt = "dkvp"
			o.oFmt = "dkvp"
			i++
			continue
		case "--json", "-j", "--j2j":
			o.iFmt = "json"
			o.oFmt = "json"
			i++
			continue
		case "--jsonl", "--l2l":

func runPipeline(o *opts, chain []Verb, files []string) error {
	reader := newReader(o)
	writer := newWriter(o)

	// Collect records into a slice first (simple; not streaming).
	var inputs []*Record
	emitFn := func(r *Record) error {
		inputs = append(inputs, r)
		return nil
	}
	if !o.noInput {
		if len(files) == 0 {
			if err := reader.Read(os.Stdin, emitFn); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		} else {
			for _, fn := range files {
				if err := readFile(reader, fn, emitFn); err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// Run verb chain.
	cur := inputs
	for _, v := range chain {
		var next []*Record
		emit := func(r *Record) { next = append(next, r) }
		for _, rec := range cur {
			v.Process(rec, emit)
		}
		v.Finish(emit)
		cur = next
	}

	// Write.
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := writer.Write(&out, cur); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err := os.Stdout.Write(out.Bytes())
	return err
}

func readFile(r Reader, fn string, emit func(*Record) error) error {
	if fn == "-" {
		return r.Read(os.Stdin, emit)
	}
	f, err := os.Open(fn)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	return r.Read(f, emit)
}

	switch o.iFmt {

	noInput   bool

func newOpts() *opts {

		},

func main() {
	args := os.Args[1:]
	if len(args) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr: no verb supplied.")
		printUsage(os.Stderr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Handle top-level "pseudo-verbs".
	switch args[0] {
	case "--version":
		fmt.Printf("mlr %s\n", version)
		return
	case "version":
		fmt.Printf("mlr version %s for %s/%s/%s\n", version, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH, "go1.24.0")
		return
	case "--help", "-h", "help":
		handleHelp(args)
		return
	case "-l":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "-L":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "-g":
		// fallback: run help flags (not fully implemented)
		return
	}

	o := newOpts()
	rest, err := parseMainFlags(o, args)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr: no verb supplied.")
		printUsage(os.Stderr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Parse verb chain.
	var chain []Verb
	var files []string
	verbArgs := rest
	for len(verbArgs) > 0 {
		verbName := verbArgs[0]
		verbArgs = verbArgs[1:]
		v, remaining, err := buildVerb(verbName, verbArgs)
		if err != nil {
			if hr, ok := err.(helpRequest); ok {
				printVerbHelp(hr.verb, os.Stdout)
				return
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr %s: %s\n", verbName, err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		chain = append(chain, v)
		// Look for "then" in remaining; otherwise remaining = files (for last verb)
		if idx := indexOf(remaining, "then"); idx >= 0 {
			// remaining[:idx] are stray (probably files only allowed after last verb).
			files = append(files, remaining[:idx]...)
			verbArgs = remaining[idx+1:]
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, remaining...)
		break
	}

	// Input files from --from / --mfrom
	allFiles := append([]string{}, o.fromFiles...)
	allFiles = append(allFiles, o.mfromFiles...)
	allFiles = append(allFiles, files...)

	if err := runPipeline(o, chain, allFiles); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())

func printUsage(w io.Writer) {
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Usage: mlr [flags] {verb} [verb-dependent options ...] {zero or more file names}")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "If zero file names are provided, standard input is read, e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv sort -f shape example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Output of one verb may be chained as input to another using \"then\", e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv stats1 -a min,mean,max -f quantity then sort -f color example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please see 'mlr help topics' for more information.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please also see https://miller.readthedocs.io")
}

func handleHelp(args []string) {
	// args[0] is "help" or "--help" etc.
	if args[0] == "--help" || args[0] == "-h" {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	if len(args) == 1 {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	topic := args[1]
	switch topic {
	case "topics":
		printHelpTopics(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "list-verbs":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "usage-verbs":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "verb":
		if len(args) < 3 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr help verb: verb name required")
			os.Exit(1)

		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint --from example.csv sort -nr index then cut -f shape,quantity")

	// Default: print usage.

func runPipeline(o *opts, chain []Verb, files []string) error {
	reader := newReader(o)
	writer := newWriter(o)

	// Collect records into a slice first (simple; not streaming).
	var inputs []*Record
	emitFn := func(r *Record) error {
		inputs = append(inputs, r)
		return nil
	}
	if !o.noInput {
		if len(files) == 0 {
			if err := reader.Read(os.Stdin, emitFn); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		} else {
			for _, fn := range files {
				if err := readFile(reader, fn, emitFn); err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// Run verb chain.
	cur := inputs
	for _, v := range chain {
		var next []*Record
		emit := func(r *Record) { next = append(next, r) }
		for _, rec := range cur {
			v.Process(rec, emit)
		}
		v.Finish(emit)
		cur = next
	}

	// Write.
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := writer.Write(&out, cur); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err := os.Stdout.Write(out.Bytes())
	return err
}

func readFile(r Reader, fn string, emit func(*Record) error) error {
	if fn == "-" {
		return r.Read(os.Stdin, emit)
	}
	f, err := os.Open(fn)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	return r.Read(f, emit)
}

	allFiles = append(allFiles, files...)

	if err := runPipeline(o, chain, allFiles); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func printUsage(w io.Writer) {
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Usage: mlr [flags] {verb} [verb-dependent options ...] {zero or more file names}")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "If zero file names are provided, standard input is read, e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv sort -f shape example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Output of one verb may be chained as input to another using \"then\", e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv stats1 -a min,mean,max -f quantity then sort -f color example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please see 'mlr help topics' for more information.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please also see https://miller.readthedocs.io")
}

func handleHelp(args []string) {
	// args[0] is "help" or "--help" etc.
	if args[0] == "--help" || args[0] == "-h" {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	if len(args) == 1 {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	topic := args[1]
	switch topic {
	case "topics":
		printHelpTopics(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "list-verbs":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "usage-verbs":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "verb":
		if len(args) < 3 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr help verb: verb name required")
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		printVerbHelp(args[2], os.Stdout)
		return
	case "basic-examples":
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint cat example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint sort -f shape example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint sort -f shape -nr index example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint cut -f flag,shape example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --csv filter '$color == \"red\"' example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --ojson put '$ratio = $quantity / $rate' example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint --from example.csv sort -nr index then cut -f shape,quantity")
		return
	}
	// Default: print usage.
	printUsage(os.Stdout)
}

func sepAlias(s string) string {
	switch s {
	case "tab", "TAB":
		return "\t"
	case "comma", "COMMA":
		return ","
	case "space", "SPACE":
		return " "
	case "semicolon", "SEMICOLON":
		return ";"
	case "pipe", "PIPE":
		return "|"
	case "colon", "COLON":
		return ":"
	case "equals", "EQUALS":
		return "="
	case "newline", "NEWLINE":
		return "\n"
	case "cr", "CR":
		return "\r"
	case "crlf", "CRLF":
		return "\r\n"
	case "lf", "LF":
		return "\n"
	}
	return s
}

// -------------------- pipeline --------------------

func runPipeline(o *opts, chain []Verb, files []string) error {
	reader := newReader(o)
	writer := newWriter(o)

	// Collect records into a slice first (simple; not streaming).
	var inputs []*Record
	emitFn := func(r *Record) error {
		inputs = append(inputs, r)
		return nil
	}
	if !o.noInput {
		if len(files) == 0 {
			if err := reader.Read(os.Stdin, emitFn); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		} else {
			for _, fn := range files {
				if err := readFile(reader, fn, emitFn); err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// Run verb chain.
	cur := inputs
	for _, v := range chain {
		var next []*Record
		emit := func(r *Record) { next = append(next, r) }
		for _, rec := range cur {
			v.Process(rec, emit)
		}
		v.Finish(emit)
		cur = next
	}

	// Write.
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := writer.Write(&out, cur); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err := os.Stdout.Write(out.Bytes())
	return err
}

func readFile(r Reader, fn string, emit func(*Record) error) error {
	if fn == "-" {
		return r.Read(os.Stdin, emit)
	}
	f, err := os.Open(fn)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	return r.Read(f, emit)
}

func newReader(o *opts) Reader {
	switch o.iFmt {
	case "csv":
		return &CSVReader{Opt: o.opt, Lite: o.csvLite, Implicit: o.implicitCSVHeader, AllowRagged: o.allowRaggedCSV, TrimLeadingSpace: o.csvTrimLS}

	case "dkvp":

	case "json":

	case "jsonl":

	case "nidx":

const (
	progName = "mlr"
	version  = "6.16.0"
)

// Global state derived from CLI flags.

type opts struct {
	iFmt string
	oFmt string
	opt  *FormatOptions

	fromFiles []string
	mfromFiles []string
	noInput   bool

	csvLite bool

	implicitCSVHeader bool

	allowRaggedCSV bool
	csvTrimLS      bool
}

func newOpts() *opts {
	return &opts{
		iFmt: "dkvp",
		oFmt: "dkvp",
		opt: &FormatOptions{
			IFS: "", IPS: "", OFS: "", OPS: "", IRS: "", ORS: "",
			Flatsep: ".",
		},
	}
}

func main() {
	args := os.Args[1:]
	if len(args) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr: no verb supplied.")
		printUsage(os.Stderr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Handle top-level "pseudo-verbs".
	switch args[0] {
	case "--version":
		fmt.Printf("mlr %s\n", version)
		return
	case "version":
		fmt.Printf("mlr version %s for %s/%s/%s\n", version, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH, "go1.24.0")
		return
	case "--help", "-h", "help":
		handleHelp(args)
		return
	case "-l":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "-L":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "-g":
		// fallback: run help flags (not fully implemented)
		return
	}

	o := newOpts()
	rest, err := parseMainFlags(o, args)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr: no verb supplied.")
		printUsage(os.Stderr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Parse verb chain.
	var chain []Verb
	var files []string
	verbArgs := rest
	for len(verbArgs) > 0 {
		verbName := verbArgs[0]
		verbArgs = verbArgs[1:]
		v, remaining, err := buildVerb(verbName, verbArgs)
		if err != nil {
			if hr, ok := err.(helpRequest); ok {
				printVerbHelp(hr.verb, os.Stdout)
				return
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr %s: %s\n", verbName, err.Error())
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		chain = append(chain, v)
		// Look for "then" in remaining; otherwise remaining = files (for last verb)
		if idx := indexOf(remaining, "then"); idx >= 0 {
			// remaining[:idx] are stray (probably files only allowed after last verb).
			files = append(files, remaining[:idx]...)
			verbArgs = remaining[idx+1:]
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, remaining...)
		break
	}

	// Input files from --from / --mfrom
	allFiles := append([]string{}, o.fromFiles...)
	allFiles = append(allFiles, o.mfromFiles...)
	allFiles = append(allFiles, files...)

	if err := runPipeline(o, chain, allFiles); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "mlr: %s\n", err.Error())
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

func printUsage(w io.Writer) {
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Usage: mlr [flags] {verb} [verb-dependent options ...] {zero or more file names}")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "If zero file names are provided, standard input is read, e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv sort -f shape example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Output of one verb may be chained as input to another using \"then\", e.g.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr --csv stats1 -a min,mean,max -f quantity then sort -f color example.csv")
	fmt.Fprintln(w)
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please see 'mlr help topics' for more information.")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Please also see https://miller.readthedocs.io")
}

func handleHelp(args []string) {
	// args[0] is "help" or "--help" etc.
	if args[0] == "--help" || args[0] == "-h" {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	if len(args) == 1 {
		printUsage(os.Stdout)
		return
	}
	topic := args[1]
	switch topic {
	case "topics":
		printHelpTopics(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "list-verbs":
		listVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "usage-verbs":
		listUsageVerbs(os.Stdout)
		return
	case "verb":
		if len(args) < 3 {
			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mlr help verb: verb name required")
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		printVerbHelp(args[2], os.Stdout)
		return
	case "basic-examples":
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint cat example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint sort -f shape example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint sort -f shape -nr index example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint cut -f flag,shape example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --csv filter '$color == \"red\"' example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --ojson put '$ratio = $quantity / $rate' example.csv")
		fmt.Println("mlr --icsv --opprint --from example.csv sort -nr index then cut -f shape,quantity")
		return
	}
	// Default: print usage.
	printUsage(os.Stdout)
}

func printHelpTopics(w io.Writer) {
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Type 'mlr help {topic}' for any of the following:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Essentials:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help topics")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help basic-examples")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help file-formats")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Verbs:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help list-verbs")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help usage-verbs")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr help verb")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "Shorthands:")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr -l = mlr help list-verbs")
	fmt.Fprintln(w, "  mlr -L = mlr help usage-verbs")
}

func listVerbs(w io.Writer) {
	verbs := []string{
		"cat",
		"check",
		"count-distinct",
		"count",
		"cut",
		"filter",
		"group-by",
		"head",
		"label",
		"nothing",
		"put",
		"regularize",
		"rename",
		"reorder",
		"skip-trivial-records",
		"sort",
		"tac",
		"tail",
		"uniq",
	}
	bw := bufio.NewWriter(w)
	defer bw.Flush()
	for _, v := range verbs {
		bw.WriteString(v)
		bw.WriteString("\n")
	}
}

func sepAlias(s string) string {
	switch s {
	case "tab", "TAB":
		return "\t"
	case "comma", "COMMA":
		return ","
	case "space", "SPACE":
		return " "
	case "semicolon", "SEMICOLON":
		return ";"
	case "pipe", "PIPE":
		return "|"
	case "colon", "COLON":
		return ":"
	case "equals", "EQUALS":
		return "="
	case "newline", "NEWLINE":
		return "\n"
	case "cr", "CR":
		return "\r"
	case "crlf", "CRLF":
		return "\r\n"
	case "lf", "LF":
		return "\n"
	}
	return s
}

func buildVerb(name string, args []string) (Verb, []string, error) {
	switch name {
	case "cat":
		return asVerb(parseCatArgs(args))
	case "head":
		return asVerb(parseHeadArgs(args))
	case "tail":
		return asVerb(parseTailArgs(args))
	case "tac":
		return asVerb(parseTacArgs(args))
	case "cut":
		return asVerb(parseCutArgs(args))
	case "sort":
		return asVerb(parseSortArgs(args))
	case "rename":
		return asVerb(parseRenameArgs(args))
	case "label":
		return asVerb(parseLabelArgs(args))
	case "uniq":
		return asVerb(parseUniqArgs(args))
	case "count":
		return asVerb(parseCountArgs(args))
	case "count-distinct":
		return asVerb(parseCountDistinctArgs(args))
	case "group-by":
		return asVerb(parseGroupByArgs(args))
	case "filter":
		return asVerb(parseFilterArgs(args))
	case "put":
		return asVerb(parsePutArgs(args))
	case "nothing":
		return asVerb(&nothingVerb{}, args, nil)
	case "check":
		return asVerb(&checkVerb{}, args, nil)
	case "reorder":
		return asVerb(parseReorderArgs(args))
	case "regularize":
		return asVerb(parseRegularizeArgs(args))
	case "skip-trivial-records":
		return asVerb(parseSkipTrivialArgs(args))
	}
	return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("verb \"%s\" not found. Please use \"mlr -l\" for a list.", name)
}

func asVerb(vi interface{}, rest ...interface{}) (Verb, []string, error) {
	// Dispatcher: if first arg is a pointer to a verb struct and next args are remaining/err,
	// or if (v, rest, err) tuple is returned from a helper.
	// This is a small shim: if called as asVerb(parseX(args)) it returns the same tuple.
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		v, _ := vi.(Verb)
		return v, nil, nil
	}
	// Not used this way currently.
	return vi.(Verb), rest[0].([]string), nil
}

func castV(v interface{}) Verb {
	if v == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if vv, ok := v.(Verb); ok {
		return vv
	}
	return nil
}

// -------------------- pipeline --------------------

func runPipeline(o *opts, chain []Verb, files []string) error {
	reader := newReader(o)
	writer := newWriter(o)

	// Collect records into a slice first (simple; not streaming).
	var inputs []*Record
	emitFn := func(r *Record) error {
		inputs = append(inputs, r)
		return nil
	}
	if !o.noInput {
		if len(files) == 0 {
			if err := reader.Read(os.Stdin, emitFn); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		} else {
			for _, fn := range files {
				if err := readFile(reader, fn, emitFn); err != nil {
					return err
				}
			}
		}
	}

	// Run verb chain.
	cur := inputs
	for _, v := range chain {
		var next []*Record
		emit := func(r *Record) { next = append(next, r) }
		for _, rec := range cur {
			v.Process(rec, emit)
		}
		v.Finish(emit)
		cur = next
	}

	// Write.
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := writer.Write(&out, cur); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err := os.Stdout.Write(out.Bytes())
	return err
}

func readFile(r Reader, fn string, emit func(*Record) error) error {
	if fn == "-" {
		return r.Read(os.Stdin, emit)
	}
	f, err := os.Open(fn)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer f.Close()
	return r.Read(f, emit)
}

func newReader(o *opts) Reader {
	switch o.iFmt {
	case "csv":
		return &CSVReader{Opt: o.opt, Lite: o.csvLite, Implicit: o.implicitCSVHeader, AllowRagged: o.allowRaggedCSV, TrimLeadingSpace: o.csvTrimLS}
	case "tsv":
		return &CSVReader{Opt: o.opt, UseTab: true, Lite: o.csvLite, Implicit: o.implicitCSVHeader, AllowRagged: o.allowRaggedCSV, TrimLeadingSpace: o.csvTrimLS}
	case "dkvp":
		return &DKVPReader{Opt: o.opt}
	case "json":
		return &JSONReader{Opt: o.opt}
	case "jsonl":
		return &JSONReader{Opt: o.opt, Lines: true}
	case "nidx":
		return &NIDXReader{Opt: o.opt}
	case "pprint":
		return &PPRINTReader{Opt: o.opt}
	case "xtab":
		return &XTABReader{Opt: o.opt}
	case "md":
		return &MDReader{Opt: o.opt}
	}
	return &DKVPReader{Opt: o.opt}
}

func newWriter(o *opts) Writer {
	switch o.oFmt {
	case "csv":
		return &CSVWriter{Opt: o.opt, Lite: o.csvLite}
	case "tsv":
		return &CSVWriter{Opt: o.opt, UseTab: true, Lite: o.csvLite}
	case "dkvp":
		return &DKVPWriter{Opt: o.opt}
	case "json":
		return &JSONWriter{Opt: o.opt}
	case "jsonl":
		return &JSONWriter{Opt: o.opt, Lines: true}
	case "nidx":
		return &NIDXWriter{Opt: o.opt}
	case "pprint":
		return &PPRINTWriter{Opt: o.opt}
	case "xtab":
		return &XTABWriter{Opt: o.opt}
	case "md":
		return &MDWriter{Opt: o.opt}
	}
	return &DKVPWriter{Opt: o.opt}
}

#!/bin/bash
# Comparison tests for my mlr
REF=./executable
MINE=/tmp/mlrtest
pass=0
fail=0
tests=()
add() { tests+=("$1"); }

compare() {
  local name="$1"
  local expected actual
  expected=$(eval "$REF $CMD" 2>&1)
  actual=$(eval "$MINE $CMD" 2>&1)
  if [ "$expected" = "$actual" ]; then
    echo "PASS: $name"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    echo "FAIL: $name"
    echo "-- expected --"
    echo "$expected" | head -10
    echo "-- actual --"
    echo "$actual" | head -10
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

DATA1=$(printf "a,b,c\n1,2,3\n4,5,6\n7,8,9\n")

CMD="--csv cat <<< '$DATA1'" compare "csv-cat"
CMD="--csv head -n 2 <<< '$DATA1'" compare "csv-head"
